bulletins.title: Imposters Threatening Phone Deactivation Under Guise of FTC
bulletins.summary: Scammers call pretending to be Federal Trade Commission agents, citing fabricated badge numbers. They claim a phone registered in the victim's name is tied to overseas fraud and threaten immediate service deactivation if the victim refuses to cooperate.

bulletins.title: Police and Official Impersonation Urging Account Transfers
bulletins.summary: Fraudsters contact consumers posing as police officers, banking staff, or trusted institutions. They use researched personal details and urgent pressure to persuade targets that their funds are at risk and must be moved or verified.

bulletins.title: Fake Charity Sweepstakes and Prize Impersonation Calls
bulletins.summary: Callers falsely claim to represent legitimate charities that the victim previously supported, announcing a sweepstakes prize win. Scammers use the charity's reputation to lower defenses and demand fees, taxes, or banking information before prizes can be released.

bulletins.title: Misleading Health Insurance and Marketplace Discount Pitches
bulletins.summary: Telemarketers and imposters exploit the open enrollment period to push deceptive healthcare plans and medical discount cards over the phone. Callers often pretend to represent the government exchange or major insurers while peddling non-compliant coverage.

gemini_context_snippet: Watch for callers claiming to be FTC agents threatening phone service deactivation over overseas fraud accusations, or police imposters demanding transfers to secure accounts. Be alert to open-enrollment health insurance sales calls pushing medical discount cards and unexpected calls claiming prizes in charity-linked sweepstakes.
